- SAS Medical Documentation
- Learning disabilities and autism spectrum disorders: Full psycho-educational assessment, memory assessment (if memory aids are required); Within the last five years (older documentation considered on a case-by-case basis).
- ADD/ADHD: Psycho-educational assessment, medical report (outlining history and areas of weakness, strength), memory assessment (if memory aids are required); Within the last five years (older documentation considered on a case-by-case basis).
- Mental health disability: Student Accessibility Services form, mental health assessment, doctor’s letter, memory assessment (if memory aids are required); Within the last five years (older documentation considered on a case-by-case basis).
- Acquired brain injury (ABI): Neuropsychological assessment; Within the last five years (older documentation considered on a case-by-case basis).
- Blind or visually impaired: Doctor’s letter, Canadian National Institute for the Blind (CNIB) registration number (if legally blind); CNIB registration date (if legally blind) or within the last five years (older documentation considered on a case-by-case basis).
- Deaf or hard of hearing: Full audiology report, doctor’s letter; Within the last five years (older documentation considered on a case-by-case basis).
- Central auditory processing disorder: Audiology report; Within the last five years (older documentation considered on a case-by-case basis).
- Chronic medical condition or physical disability: Student Accessibility Services form, mental health assessment, doctor’s letter; Within the last five years (older documentation considered on a case-by-case basis).

registration_process:
Step 1. Complete the Intake Form - ( Log in to MySAS Portal - Click “Accommodation” in the menu on the left - Click “Intake Request” in the menu. Then, select “Form.” - Complete the intake form. Make sure to fill out all the required fields - Before submitting, go back to make sure that your information is accurate. Also, check that all the required fields are complete - Save and submit your request - Next, we’ll email you to upload your documentation - Please upload your documentation within 12 calendar days)

Step 2. Upload your documentation - (Log in to MySAS Portal - Click “Accommodation” in the menu on the left - Click “Documents” in the menu - Upload your documentation or assessment of functional impairment (AFI) - Click save and submit your request)

Step 3. Book an intake appointment - (Log in to MySAS Portal - Click “Appointment” in the menu on the left - Request a new appointment by completing the form - Choose “Intake” from the list of appointment types - Review and select a time. We recommend checking your calendar and timetable first. Appointments can be virtual or in person. Note: All appointments take place Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. - Confirm your appointment.)

Step 4. Meet your program coordinator - (Log in to MySAS Portal - Click “Appointment” in the menu on the left - View your appointment details in the “Approved Appointments” section on the right)

Step 5. Receive your accommodation plan - (Log in to MySAS Portal - Click “Appointment” in the menu on the left - Click “Accommodation Letter/Emails” in the menu - Review your letter of accommodation)

osap_eligibility:
To apply for full-time OSAP aid, you must:
 • register in full-time studies for the session 
 • be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or have protected person status; international students are ineligible.
 • have Ontario residency, that is, have lived in Ontario for at least 12 consecutive months without attending full-time postsecondary school.
 • register in an OSAP-approved degree program. Most degree programs at York are OSAP approved.
 • be neither in default on a previous OSAP student loan nor on OSAP restriction.
 • maintain satisfactory academic progress while receiving OSAP aid.
 • have demonstrated financial need as calculated by the government. Gross family income as well as student resources and assets are taken into consideration.

 • be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or have protected person status; international students are ineligible.
 • have Ontario residency, that is, have lived in Ontario for at least 12 consecutive months without attending full-time postsecondary school.
 • register in an OSAP-approved degree program. Most degree programs at York are OSAP approved.
 • be neither in default on a previous OSAP student loan nor on OSAP restriction.
 • maintain satisfactory academic progress while receiving OSAP aid.
 • have demonstrated financial need as calculated by the government. Gross family income as well as student resources and assets are taken into consideration.

registration_process:
STEP 1: Complete the SAS Application Form - What you need to complete the application: Currently enrolled or accepted an offer of admission, Have a U of G Username and log-in credentials, Have a Student ID, Current students can apply at any time of the semester
STEP 2: Submit Your Documentation - Documentation can be included at the time of applying or uploaded later using the customized link sent by email. Submissions will be processed as quickly as possible to ensure fall semester accommodations are in place as soon as possible. Some restrictions on accommodations may apply depending on academic deadlines throughout each semester. You will be required to submit documentation from a registered health professional which verifies the existence of a disability and describes your current functional abilities given the condition you experience. 
STEP 3: Book Your Intake Appointment with your SAS Advisor - After submitting your application, use the portal to book an intake appointment using the SAS Student Portal 
STEP 4: Apply for OSAP or Financial Support - Mark "Disability" on Your Application - (If you're applying for OSAP and have a documented disability, check the disability box. This could help you qualify for extra supports like the Bursary for Students with Disabilities (BSWD).)
Step 5: Attend a Summer Orientation Event - Various accessibility events are hosted during the summer (June - September) to help first-year undergrads, returning, transfer and graduate students understand how SAS works. If you are attending the University of Guelph for the first time in the Fall semester, be sure to check out our Orientation Events page to help you navigate your first year with SAS. 
Step 6: Request Your Accommodations - Once registered with SAS, go to the SAS Portal to send your accommodation letters to instructors using the SAS Student Portal . You’ll need to do this every semester for each course.
Step 7: Communicate with Instructors - Discuss Your Accommodations (if needed)

- Acquired Brain Injury (ABI): copy of a recent neuro-psychological assessment, PMC Documentation of Acquired Brain Injury Form completed by a regulated healthcare professional
- Attention deficit / Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD): copy of your latest comprehensive psychoeducational assessment (completed by a registered psychologist or psychological associate), an assessment completed within the last 5 years (or at the age of 18 years or older), PMC Documentation of ADHD Form completed by a regulated health care practitioner
- Autism Spectrum Disorders: Psycho-educational assessment (PEA) (completed within the last 5 years or performed using adult-normed tests), PMC ASD documentation Form (completed by a regulated health care practitioner who can confirm diagnosis and provide information on current functional limitations)
- Chronic Medical Conditions: PMC Documentation of Medical Disability Form (completed by a regulated health care professional is preferred), If it is not possible to get this form completed in time for your intake appointment, we will accept other medical documents that confirm that nature of your disability and functional impairments relevant to the university setting as interim documentation.
- Deaf and Hard of Hearing: recent audiogram or audiology assessment report, AND PMC Documentation of Hearing Impairment Form (completed by an otolaryngologist, audiologist or treating family physician)
- Learning Disabilities (LD): recent Psycho-Educational Assessment (PEA) (completed by a registered psychologist or psychological associate within the last 5 years or at the age of 18 years or older is preferred)
- Mobility/Physical Disabilities: PMC Documentation of Mobility Disability Form (completed by a regulated health care professional)
- Mental Health Disabilities: PMC Documentation of Mental Health Disability Form (completed by a regulated health care professional who has knowledge of the student’s history and is licensed to diagnose and treat mental health disorders), copy of a recent psychological assessment report completed by a registered psychologist or psychological associate
- Blind and Partially Sighted: PMC Documentation of Vision Impairment Form (completed by an ophthalmologist, optometrist, low vision specialist or treating family physician)

Step 2: Create a Ventus student account - You will be required to create a Ventus student account prior to your intake appointment.Ventus is a one-stop academic accommodation management tool to help you manage and keep track of your accommodations in your courses.
Step 3: Complete the AFI and Intake Consent From - You will receive a confirmation email to your CMAIL with details of your appointment 1-3 business days prior to your scheduled appointment. The email will include instructions on the completion of the Intake Consent Form and the Assessment of Functional Impairment (AFI) questionnaire which must be completed prior to your appointment. 
Step 4: Submit your documentation before your appointment - Your disability documentation can be uploaded directly to Ventus where your PMC Coordinator will be able to review the information.
Step 5: FIVE: Attend your intake appointment - When requesting an intake appointment, you have the options of selecting an in-person or a virtual meeting with a PMC Coordinator. (If you’re attending an in-person intake appointment, please note that the Paul Menton Centre is located in Room 501 of the Nideyinàn Building (NN). registration_process:
Step 1: Collect Your Documentation - Once you have accepted an offer of admission to Lakehead University, gather your documentation of a permanent or temporary disability and/or medical condition. You can email, fax or drop off your documentation, or bring it with you to your appointment with Student Accessibility Services. For more information on documentation please visit our webpage on documentation. (If you do not have any documentation, or are unsure if your documentation is sufficient you can skip to Step 2 and connect with SAS to discuss documentation.)
Step 2: Connect With SAS - Once you have registered in your classes, connect with SAS to schedule an appointment to set up accommodations and start the registration process. (this appointment can take place as early as late June or July)
If you are unable to meet in person, email or phone SAS to request a phone or video appointment.
Step 3: Activate Your Term Accommodations - Prior to the term start date SAS will email you with instructions on how to activate your accommodations for the term. You will need to complete this process each and every term for which you require accommodations. (SAS Staff will process your accommodation request and send your accommodation form(s) to your instructors. You will receive a copy of the email that goes to your instructors in your Lakehead University email inbox. The Accommodation Form will be attached to the email. Save this form to your computer for your future reference. Once you receive these emails your accommodations are active for the term.)
Step 4: Participate in SAS Procedures - Students requesting or registered with academic accommodations through Student Accessibility Services (SAS) have a duty to participate in the accommodation process by following SAS timeline requests: including but not limited to regularly checking your @lakeheadu.ca student email, completing the accommodation request form at the beginning of each term, booking tests, or requesting alternate dates/start times for tests according to the SAS timelines.

To qualify for OSAP at Lakehead University, you generally must meet the following:

Ontario Resident: You must be an Ontario resident, determined by criteria such as having lived in Ontario for the past 12 consecutive months, not including time spent as a full-time post-secondary student.

Citizenship/Status: You must be a Canadian citizen, Permanent Resident of Canada, or a Protected Person. International students are not eligible for OSAP.

No Fraud/Theft Conviction: You are ineligible if convicted of fraud or theft related to any student financial assistance program in Canada.

osap_eligibility:
Laurentian University, situated in Sudbury, Ontario, adheres to the provincial guidelines for the Ontario Student Assistance Program (OSAP). This means the core eligibility criteria for OSAP funding are the same for students at Laurentian as they are for students at any other publicly funded post-secondary institution in Ontario.

General OSAP Eligibility
To be eligible for OSAP at Laurentian University, you must typically meet the following requirements:

Ontario Resident: You must be an Ontario resident. This is generally defined by having lived in Ontario for at least 12 consecutive months, not including time spent as a full-time post-secondary student.


Citizenship/Status: You must be a Canadian citizen, Permanent Resident of Canada, or a Protected Person. International students are not eligible for OSAP.

Approved Program of Study: You must be enrolled in an OSAP-approved program that leads to a degree, diploma, or certificate. Most undergraduate, Master's, and Doctoral programs at Laurentian are approved. If you are in a non-degree program or certain specialized certificate programs, it's best to confirm eligibility with Laurentian's Student Awards Office.

Eligible Course Load: Your registration must meet the minimum requirements for either full-time or part-time OSAP.

Good Standing: You must not be in default on any previous OSAP loans or have any restrictions on your OSAP account.

Satisfactory Academic Progress: You need to maintain satisfactory academic progress in your program of study.

Financial Need: Your application will be assessed based on your and your family's (if applicable) financial situation to determine your financial need.

Lifetime Funding Limit: You must not have exceeded the lifetime limit of student loan funding (typically 340 weeks for most students, 400 weeks for doctoral students, or up to 520 weeks for students with a permanent disability).

First-Time Applicant Module: If you are a full-time or micro-credential student making your first OSAP application for the 2024–2025 or 2025–2026 school year, you will be required to complete an interactive financial literacy module.
